title: select filtering sorting and pagination
concepts: A SELECT query describes which rows and columns belong in a result. The written clause order is not the same as logical query processing order, so aliases and predicates are visible only at specific stages; filtering, projection, sorting, and row limiting should be reasoned about separately.

A WHERE search condition is evaluated using SQL's three-valued logic: TRUE, FALSE, and UNKNOWN. NULL is not an ordinary value, so equality with NULL does not test for missing data; use IS NULL or the null-safe IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM predicate where appropriate.

ORDER BY is the only guarantee of result ordering. TOP limits rows before a client receives them, while OFFSET/FETCH expresses a page range within ORDER BY. Pagination needs a deterministic ordering key and a strategy for concurrent data changes; large offsets can be more costly than a continuation-key approach.

Pattern matching has different tools: LIKE handles a compact wildcard grammar and collation-sensitive comparisons, while SQL Server 2025 REGEXP_LIKE provides regular-expression matching at database compatibility level 170 or higher. Their semantics and indexability differ.
SQL Server syntax is not identical to every T-SQL host. Features documented only for Microsoft Fabric, such as ORDER BY ALL and QUALIFY, must not be taught as SQL Server syntax.

versionNotes.edition: SQL Server 2022 and SQL Server 2025 SELECT predicate additions
items: SQL Server 2022 added IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM for equality comparisons that always return TRUE or FALSE even when either operand is NULL. SQL Server 2025 added REGEXP_LIKE for regular-expression filtering; it requires database compatibility level 170 and does not follow collation rules. These are focused additions: the core SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, TOP, and OFFSET/FETCH clause forms remain the basis of the topic.

scopeExclusions: FROM joins, APPLY, and PIVOT are taught in t03-004; this topic includes only the FROM and table-alias context needed to teach projection and filtering.
GROUP BY, HAVING, aggregate functions, and window functions belong to t03-005; HAVING appears here only as a comparison with row-level WHERE filtering.
INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, and bulk operations are taught in t03-006. TOP on data-modification statements is out of scope.
Index design and access paths, SARGability analysis, execution plans, and query tuning are taught in t03-008, t03-009, and t03-013; REGEXP_LIKE indexability is mentioned only as a predicate boundary.
SQL Server 2025 regular-expression scalar and table-valued functions other than the REGEXP_LIKE predicate are outside this selection/filtering topic.
ORDER BY ALL and QUALIFY are named only to mark their Microsoft Fabric boundary; they are not SQL Server syntax and must not be taught as available SQL Server features.
Keyset pagination is introduced as a design alternative; indexing and application cursor-token implementation details are covered in their own topics.
